Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Power Utilities Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Power Utilities' Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer; David Kim, Chief Strategy Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1. O&M expense management initiatives and efficiency gains.
    2. Storm response and recovery efforts.
    3. Generation fleet performance and availability.
    4. Customer growth and usage trends across residential, commercial, and industrial segments.
    5. Authorized versus earned Return on Equity analysis.
    6. Forward-looking statements and implications for our growth.

These elements highlight our operational resilience and financial discipline across our 25 GW generation portfolio and service to 2.8 million customers. Michael will provide deeper insights into these areas as part of the financial review. Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss the financials.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. For the third quarter, we reported earnings per share of $1.05 and revenue of $3.25 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $720 million, primarily focused on renewable expansions and grid hardening initiatives. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate continued EPS growth of 7 to 9% in fiscal 2025.

Let me expand on the key drivers Sarah mentioned, starting with our O&M expense management initiatives and efficiency gains. We continue to demonstrate disciplined execution amid a challenging macroeconomic backdrop. O&M represents about 28% of our total operating expenses this quarter, down from 32% a year ago, reflecting the structural efficiencies we've embedded across our 25 GW regulated and competitive generation portfolio. Consolidated O&M came in at $425 million, a 7.2% year-over-year decline, or roughly $32 million below our guidance midpoint. On a trailing twelve-month basis, we've reduced O&M intensity by 9.5%, now at $18.42 per MWh generated compared to $20.37 per MWh last year. This not only offset 4.1% inflation in labor and materials but also generated $115 million in incremental free cash flow year-to-date, supporting our $1.2 billion share repurchase authorization and the 4.8% dividend increase we announced today.

Breaking it down, in our thermal fleet—60% of capacity, mainly combined-cycle gas turbines and a legacy coal unit in the Midwest—O&M expenses fell 11% year-over-year to $210 million. This was driven by a 2.3% improvement in fleet-wide heat rate to 7,650 Btu/kWh through our turbine optimization program. We've deployed Siemens' MindSphere IoT platform across 12 of our 18 CCGTs, enabling real-time blade monitoring and predictive maintenance that cut unplanned outages by 18%, from 4.2% equivalent availability last year to 3.4% this quarter. This aligns with peer experiences like NextEra Energy's digital twins yielding 10-15% O&M leverage. In PJM, where 40% of our thermal output is located, we've leveraged locational marginal pricing volatility following Winter Storm Elliott by dispatching units with sub-5-minute ramp rates, boosting merchant margins by 12% while holding variable O&M steady.

Fuel management was key: our hedging secured 85% of 2024 natural gas needs at $3.25 per MMBtu, below the NYMEX strip average of $3.80, saving $28 million year-to-date. We've also tested on-site LNG regasification at Florida plants to hedge Gulf Coast pipeline issues, similar to challenges Dominion Energy faced last winter.

For renewables—now 28% of capacity, targeting 40% by 2027 under our net-zero pathway—O&M declined 6.8% to $85 million despite 15% capacity additions, including 1.2 GW of wind in the Plains and solar in the Southwest. Capacity factors remained at 38% for wind and 26% for solar PV, but per-MWh O&M dropped 14% to $12.10 per MWh via our Zero-Touch O&M initiative. This features drone-based thermographic inspections with FLIR systems, reducing tower climbs by 65% and vegetation management costs by 22% in ERCOT post-Uri reforms. SCADA upgrades inspired by Orsted on Texas wind farms use AI-driven curtailment forecasting to cut shadow losses, lifting annual energy production by 3.2%.

In transmission and distribution, serving 2.8 million customers in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic, O&M was flat sequentially at $130 million but down 5% year-over-year. Grid modernization capex synergies, including $150 million in smart meters under Inflation Reduction Act incentives, reduced non-technical losses by 8% and enabled dynamic line rating tech from Quanta Services, boosting 500 kV line capacity by 12% in ISO-NE. We contained labor costs—up 5.2% industry-wide per EEI—through our Skills Forward program, cross-training 1,200 lineworkers on EV maintenance and IBEW apprenticeships for a 9% productivity gain without headcount increases.

Regionally, Southeast Hurricane Idalia remnants were managed with mutual aid from Duke Energy and FPL, limiting restoration to 48 hours and incremental O&M to $12 million versus peers' $25 million average. Midwest coal benefited from MISO auction premiums, idling 300 MW baseload for peaker conversions, cutting fixed O&M 22% via remote monitoring. In Texas, ERCOT co-optimization rewarded battery-hybrid solar, with co-located BESS reducing degradation costs 30%.

Our asset performance management system, using GE Vernova's APM software with 50,000 sensors, projects $180 million in annualized savings by 2025—a 4x ROI on $45 million invested. We outperform S&P Global utility median by 250 bps on O&M as percent of revenues at 22.4%. We expect 6-8% further deleveraging in 2024, handling EPA coal ash rules via dry-stack and CCUS pilots for 45Q credits. This boosts ROIC to 9.8% from 9.2% and supports 10% EPS CAGR.

Risks include labor inflation over 4%, HVDC supply chains, and FERC Order 2222 delays, but five quarters of beats affirm our $1.65-$1.70 billion full-year guidance.

Next, our storm response and recovery efforts around Hurricane Zeta, which hit the Southeast on September 15 as a Category 3 with 120 mph winds and 12-foot surges in coastal Georgia and the Carolinas. NOAA notes 25% higher Atlantic hurricane intensity over the decade, testing our resilience.

Zeta impacted 1.47 million of our 2.8 million customers, peaking at 85% outages with downed lines, flooded substations, and 45,000 damaged poles—scale like Hurricane Isaias, but with 150 mph gusts in Jacksonville.

Our Storm Ready playbook, refined post-Ida and Ian, mobilized 4,200 personnel including 2,100 mutual aid from Southern Company, Entergy, and FPL. We used 150 bucket trucks, 75 tree crews, 42 LiDAR/thermal drones cutting scouting 60%, and AI outage systems with SCADA/ADMS from DroneDeploy and Esri. We prioritized critical loads: 100% hospitals, police, water within 24 hours per FEMA.

Restoration: 55% in 24 hours, 92% by 72, full by day 7—beating 5-day target, improving SAIDI 28% vs. 450-minute average. Florida at 88% in 48 hours via undergrounding 35% coastal lines since 2020; Carolinas 85% amid flooding, aided by 20 MW Tesla Megapack microgrids for 15,000 customers.

Costs: $285 million gross, $210 million opex, $75 million capex. Recoverable 82% or $234 million via Florida clause (10.25% ROE adder), $60 million insurance post-$50 million deductible, and riders. Net hit $51 million or $0.12 EPS, absorbed without guidance change. Comparable to NextEra's Ian proportionally.

Trends: storm capex up 18% CAGR since 2019 per RMS models. Vegetation outages up 22% YoY, addressed with $180 million LiDAR trimming for 40% cycle cuts.

Our $3.5 billion 5-year resiliency plan adds 500 miles undergrounding, 100 MW BESS with Fluence, AMI to 95%. Texas Oncor pilots GE Grid Orchestrator for DERs (12% peak). Georgia rider gives 9.5% ROE on $800 million, NPV $1.2 billion.

Q4 insurance $120 million boosts FCF to $1.8 billion. We push FERC for storm normalization. Reliability top-quartile per J.D. Power supports 16x P/E.

Turning to generation fleet performance and availability across our 25,000 MW, 45 units. First-half EAF 92.8%, up 180 bps from 91%, beating 92% target with EFOR down 15% to 4.2%, forced outages 1,200 hours amid polar vortex and heat domes.

CCGT fleet (55%, 13,800 MW, GE 7HA.02/Siemens SGT6-8000H) hit 95.6% EAF, 62% capacity factor (up from 58%), heat rate 6,650 Btu/kWh via inlet cooling and AspenTech digital twins cutting startups 20%. ERCOT South Texas at 68% in summer peaks, $45/MWh spreads.

Coal (10%, 2,500 MW post-2023 retirements) 91% availability; Powder River CFB overhaul lifted efficiency to 38%. Midwest 600 MW blends 20% hydrogen with Air Products, no NOx hit, 5% heat rate gain.

Nuclear (2,200 MW Northeast) 93.2% capacity factor, best in five years vs. NEI 91.5%; 22-day outages with Framatome GAIA fuel. ISO-NE baseload 100% in cold snap.

Renewables (35%, 8,750 MW, 60/40 wind/solar) 98.5% availability; wind 36% (Vestas/GE) down 2 pts SPP winds, solar 27% CAISO clouds. 400 MW/1,600 MWh BESS at 92% efficiency, 15% arbitrage lift.

PJM gas/nuclear >94% EAF, $35/MWh LMP; ERCOT gas 97% Level 3 alerts; WECC hydro de-rates to 88%, pumped storage 95%.

$150 million YTD in GE Predix/ABB predictive analytics cut outages 22%; Reliability 2025 drones 80% wind, NERC CIP-014. Offshore 300 MW Virginia COD 2027.

Focus on dispatchable clean: retire 1 GW coal 2025, add 1.5 GW peaker gas CCUS-ready. $400 million 500 MW Texas battery buy. FY EAF 93.5%, renewables 5-7% lift.

This fuels 8-10% EPS growth.

On customer growth and usage trends, we added 1.8% YoY or 50,000 net customers to 2.8 million, beating EEI 1.1% via Sun Belt migration. Weather-normalized sales up 2.4% to 28.5 TWh, peak 18.2 GW +4%.

Residential (72%, 2 million, +2.1% or 42,000 adds): usage +0.8% to 1,045 kWh/month, sales 19.8 TWh +2.9%. EV +35% (120,000), Nexus Charge 15,000 chargers TOU shave 15-20% peak. Heat pumps +12% EnergyWise 45,000 retrofits. Southeast +2.6%, Midwest 0.9%. DER VPP Tesla 8,000 Powerwalls 40 MW, AMI 92% cuts peak 8%.

Commercial (22%, 620,000, +1.2% 7,400 adds): usage +1.5% 2.8 MWh/month, sales 5.2 TWh +2.7%. Texas Permian +4%, Florida tourism +3%. Behind-meter solar +25% 450 MW; VPP Schneider 2,500 sites 25 MW DR. EV fleets. Forecast 1.5-2% growth, $500M reconductoring.

Industrial (6% customers, 25% margins, +1.6% 1,400 adds): sales +5.2% 3.5 TWh, usage +3.6% 28 MWh/month. Texas hyperscalers 1.2 GW, FAANG $10B Dallas, miners. Chemicals +7%, steel. Data centers 450 MW PUE 1.3. 99.999% reliability, 100 MW BESS. 4-6% growth.

Electrification/AI flattens curves; 15% PJM margin, ERCOT vigilance. Grid Optimizer AI Siemens forecasts DERs. JD Power 82/100. Guide 2.5-3% sales, rate cases.

Now, authorized vs. earned ROE for our regulated 85% of $18.2B rate base. Authorized 10.25% post-2023 dockets MISO/PJM, up 25 bps.

Q3 earned 9.45%, +40 bps YoY, 80 bps gap. WACC 7.8% vs. 8.2% embedded.

TTM: T&D (60%) auth 10.50%, earned 9.75% (+35 bps); lag on $1.2B capex HTLS. Gen (25%) auth 9.75%, earned 8.90% fuel volatility; BESS AFUDC. Renew (15%) auth 10.75%, earned 9.60% PTC offset IRA credits.

5-year up from 8.75% to 9.45%, beat EEI 9.2%. Drivers: lag 50%, opex/fuel 30%, capex 20%.

Close to 20 bps 2025: Q1 cases $1.8B, ROE Bridge digital twins 50 bps lift, PJM RTEP $600M 11% ROE. Load 4.5% CAGR, earned 9.85% 2025, 10.10% 2026.

Finally, forward-looking statements per PSLRA safe harbor; risks in 10-K/Q.

FY25 adj EPS $4.65-$4.85, up from $4.50-$4.75 on load/power prices. Revenue $12.8-$13.2B +5-7%, regulated 65%. Capex $2.7-$3.0B: 45% renewables 1.1 GW solar/BESS, 30% T&D, nuclear.

Renewables pipeline 8 GW, 60% carbon-free 2030. Offshore 300 MW GE. Merchant EBITDA $450-550M ERCOT gas.

PJM BRA $270/MW-day, ERCOT batteries 15-20% IRR. MISO JV $200M. CA LCFS.

Demand 15% CAGR EIA, rate base $28B 2027. Grid-edge VPP 500 MW. Risks rates 4.2x debt, HALEU, FERC. 5-7% EPS, 60-70% FCF return.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. On operations, we're seeing improved efficiency in our combined-cycle gas turbine power plants due to digital twin optimization implementations. This has resulted in a 12% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 20%.

David Kim: Thank you, Lisa. For long-term strategy, we're exploring battery storage opportunities. This will drive future growth. We're evaluating acquisitions in the Texas market.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, David. Technologically, we're investing in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We recently deployed an AI-driven threat detection platform to strengthen defenses against cyber threats.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Michael, Lisa, David, and Elena. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for renewable portfolio growth?

Sarah Thompson: Certainly, John. Our renewables now at 28% of capacity are on track to 40% by 2027, with 1.1 GW additions next year including solar in Southeast and BESS in California. We've integrated drone inspections and AI forecasting to boost AEP by over 3%, while IRA credits enhance returns. This aligns with our net-zero path and hyperscaler demand.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Johnson: What is your outlook for capex plans?

Michael Chen: Thanks, Emily. Capex at $2.7 to $3.0 billion for FY25 focuses 45% on renewables for 1.1 GW net adds, 30% T&D hardening, and nuclear extensions. This grows rate base 6-7% CAGR, supported by strong FCF and 85% hedged merchant exposure, positioning for ROE expansion.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Robert Lee: How are you mitigating risks related to extreme weather?

Lisa Patel: Great question, Robert. Our Storm Ready playbook and $3.5 billion resiliency plan preposition crews, deploy drones for 60% faster assessments, and add microgrids/BESS for critical loads. Post-Zeta, 92% restoration in 72 hours beat targets, with 82% cost recovery. Ongoing undergrounding and LiDAR trimming target top-quartile reliability.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in Q3, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Apex Power Utilities for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Apex Power Utilities.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
